claims.statement: The current consolidated Polish Public Procurement Law requires public construction contracts to specify contractor-payment rules conditioned on evidence that due subcontractor and further-subcontractor remuneration was paid.

Article 465 requires direct payment only for eligible accepted or submitted subcontract arrangements after nonpayment, with contractor comment, possible denial or court deposit and fact-specific proof of entitlement.

GDDKiA identifies unreadable copies, inconsistent contract and invoice references, missing evidence, unauthorized signatures, late amendments and unregistered subcontract arrangements as causes that block or delay payment requests.
For its 2014-2020 programme, GDDKiA reported more than 1,800 accepted direct-payment cases worth over 562m PLN and nearly 1,100 further applications leading contractors to pay over 353m PLN.
Polish procurement under the Public Procurement Law reached about 330.4bn PLN in 2024, with construction works representing 39% of awarded value.

The free government PEF platform already supports structured public-procurement invoices and related documents through web tools and API, although internal approval workflows remain in each authority's systems.

PlanRadar, PROGPOL and Archdesk already cover document control, approvals, subcontractor records, acceptance protocols, invoices and construction payment workflows, with PlanRadar listing plans from EUR 26 to EUR 129 per internal user monthly.
GDDKiA treats contractor and subcontractor employee data as GDPR-governed project data and recognizes IT processors, access rights, correction and retention obligations.

contrary_evidence: PEF is a free government channel for structured invoices and related public-procurement documents, reducing the value of a generic submission portal.
PlanRadar, Archdesk and Polish PROGPOL already offer document control, approvals, subcontractor records and invoice-to-acceptance workflows.
Article 465 entitlement is fact-specific and includes contractor objections, denial and court-deposit branches that cannot be safely reduced to an automated ready/not-ready legal answer.

PlanRadar's published EUR 26-129 per-user monthly pricing challenges the original 1,500-7,000 PLN per-project monthly range unless the Polish payment-proof specialization creates measurable incremental value.
GDDKiA's large direct-payment figures validate the problem but are historical, road-program-specific and include contractor financial failure, not only document defects.

economics.acquisition_route: Use one permissioned family-business project only to build and test a single-authority, single-contract-form rules pack, then seek one paid embedding pilot with an incumbent ERP/DMS vendor or multi-project contract administrator already serving that same form family. No reviewed evidence establishes partner interest, access, commitment, conversion, or a repeatable channel.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Not yet quantifiable from the reviewed evidence. A path would require a portfolio module to win enough recurring partner deployments, retain customers across project turnover, and generate founder-owned cash flow or equity value without double-counting retained earnings; partner count, portfolio size, price, margin, ownership and timing are all unvalidated.
economics.founder_time: A narrowly scoped rules-pack prototype may fit the founder's maximum 25-hour workweek only if qualified counsel owns legal interpretation and the channel partner owns implementation access and end-customer onboarding. Actual integration, support and partner-sales hours are unknown.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unknown. Reusing one counsel-approved rules pack across a partner portfolio could amortize legal configuration and onboarding, but enterprise integration, version maintenance, support, security review and partner economics could preserve service-like costs; no observed delivery-cost or margin data exist.
economics.payback: Unknown. The architecture replaces repeated project acquisition with a larger partner sale and portfolio reuse, but no evidence establishes partner sales-cycle length, implementation cost, revenue share, activation, renewal or customer acquisition payback.
economics.pricing: Unknown. Test a paid implementation plus recurring portfolio or platform licensing tied to active projects or payment-review usage, but no reviewed source validates an amount, buyer budget, partner margin, minimum commitment or premium over incumbent functionality.
economics.retention_or_repeat: A maintained embedded rules pack could remain active across successive projects in one partner's portfolio rather than ending with each project, but renewal depends on partner adoption, continued authority/form coverage, rules maintenance and measurable payment-workflow value; none is observed.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A versioned, counsel-approved rules pack and regression test suite for one authority and contract-form family can improve from permissioned exception and cure labels across a channel partner's portfolio, but reuse rights and access to any de-identified corpus must be contractually established.
fingerprint.customer: Construction ERP/DMS vendors and multi-project contract-administrator firms serving Polish contractors under one selected high-volume public-works authority and contract-form family
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed the module through one paid incumbent ERP/DMS or contract-administrator partnership that already reaches a portfolio using the selected authority/form; the family-business project is only a permissioned test environment, and no channel commitment is assumed.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: An embeddable source-linked exception rules API and user-interface module for one authority/contract-form family, maintained under qualified specialist approval and sold as implementation plus recurring portfolio/platform licensing; it does not store authoritative records or decide legal entitlement.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The ERP/DMS vendor or multi-project contract administrator pays for implementation and recurring portfolio access when the approved module is deployed across its supported projects and runs source-linked pre-submission exception checks.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An incumbent vendor or administrator repeatedly supports payment draws across projects using the same authority and contract-form family, but lacks a maintained, source-linked exception ruleset that can be reused before submission.

founder_fit: The founder's renewable-installation family access can supply a lawful permissioned test environment for one authority/form pack, but it is neither an incumbent partnership nor evidence of external demand.
Rules APIs, evidence graphs, extraction, regression tests and exception analytics match the founder's data-science and AI strengths and can be scoped to the existing 60,000 PLN validation budget.

Portfolio reuse could reduce repeated project onboarding, but the work fits the founder's 25-hour weekly ceiling only if counsel owns legal interpretation and the partner owns end-customer onboarding and first-line support.

Partner-led distribution avoids camera-based promotion and many direct contractor sales, but winning and maintaining a small number of high-trust incumbent relationships remains socially and commercially demanding.

redesign.economic_effect: Moves legal configuration, implementation and acquisition from each individual project to a versioned single-authority rules pack embedded once per channel partner and reused across that partner's portfolio. This can amortize counsel and integration work and replace project-close reacquisition with portfolio renewal, but partner conversion, reuse rights, price, margins, activation and renewal remain unvalidated.

risks: Users may mistake an exception status for a legal-entitlement decision; every ruleset and output boundary requires qualified specialist approval, source links and explicit administrative-only wording.
The selected authority and contract-form family may still vary by project or amendment enough to require costly bespoke review and maintenance.
No incumbent vendor or administrator may accept the integration, expose the needed records, fund implementation or distribute the module to its customers.
A channel partner can delay the sale, demand most of the economics, copy the narrow feature, bundle an alternative or terminate access.
PEF, KSeF, PlanRadar, Archdesk, PROGPOL and other systems can absorb or commoditize source-linked exception checking.
Permission to process sensitive project data does not imply permission to reuse de-identified exception or cure labels across a portfolio.
Personal and commercially sensitive records require granular roles, processing agreements, retention controls, audit logs and partner-compatible security review.
A family-access test and one design partner could create concentrated, non-representative evidence about demand, integration effort and portfolio reuse.
Enterprise partner acquisition and ongoing integration support may exceed the founder's part-time capacity before portfolio economics are demonstrated.

structure.commercial_archetype: Embedded B2B2B payment-evidence rules module sold through an incumbent construction-system or administrator portfolio
structure.control_point: The reusable pre-submission exception pass inside a partner's existing workflow for payment draws governed by one authority and contract-form family
structure.critical_dependency: A qualified specialist must approve and maintain the narrow rules pack, while at least one incumbent partner must authorize integration, data access and distribution without the module claiming legal entitlement; none of those partner commitments or reuse rights is established.

thesis: Build a versioned payment-evidence exception module for one selected high-volume Polish public-works authority and one contract-form family, then embed it inside an ERP/DMS vendor's or contract administrator's existing workflow. The module links authoritative records already held in PEF/KSeF and incumbent systems, runs counsel-approved administrative checks before submission and routes source-linked exceptions without deciding entitlement. Narrowing the rules surface and selling through a portfolio channel changes the cost unit from bespoke configuration and acquisition for every project to one maintained pack and integration reused across successive projects. Officially documented evidence defects support the workflow need, while free government infrastructure and capable incumbents make the embedded, non-storage posture necessary; partner demand, integration rights, price, reuse permission and resulting economics remain unknown.
title: Embedded Single-Authority Payment Evidence Module
uncertainties: Frequency, delay days and cash value of payment holds caused primarily by remediable evidence gaps
Which single authority and contract-form family has enough repeated projects and sufficiently stable rules to support reuse
Whether an ERP/DMS vendor or multi-project administrator owns budget and will enter a paid embedding pilot
External willingness to pay, partner margin expectations and an acceptable portfolio-pricing unit
Variation across projects and amendments within the selected form family and the legal-review hours required for initial and ongoing maintenance
Whether partner and project participants will authorize integration and share pricing, bank, amendment and dispute records under appropriately scoped permissions
Integration feasibility with PEF, KSeF and the selected partner's ERP/DMS stack
Measured reduction in administrator labor, rejected draws or days to payment
Partner sales cycle, activation across its portfolio, renewal, support burden, payback and mature gross margin
Whether permissioned exception and cure labels can be de-identified and contractually reused across partner projects
Whether one narrow rules pack remains valuable rather than being copied, bundled or bypassed by the incumbent channel
